speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you are an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, are you shorter than your peers, and have you ever had a fracture from a minor fall or injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (specifically 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency or non-classic form with ambiguous genitalia presentation).

The history of clitoromegaly and ambiguous genitalia at birth, combined with delayed menarche, severe acne, and fractures (suggestive of osteoporosis from long-term androgen exposure or associated enzyme defects), points strongly toward a specific form of CAH. I will confirm the diagnosis by requesting hormonal and genetic testing.

REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, Serum electrolytes, 17-ketosteroids, and ACTH stimulation test.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Xray (to assess for osteoporosis/fractures).
